title: Stakeholder Pushback on a Clarifying Question
one_liner: You ask a basic clarifying question in a workshop. The senior stakeholder pushes back: "shouldn't you already know that?"
brief:
## The room

Second requirements workshop on the partner-portal project. The lead business stakeholder is Liane, the Director of Partner Relations. She's been in the role twelve years. She's also been described to you, twice, as "someone who suffers fools more than she should but eventually doesn't".

## The moment

You ask: "when a partner is offboarded, what happens to their historical transaction data?" A reasonable question. Half the room nods.

Liane looks up. "Shouldn't you already know that? It's in every onboarding doc we've sent over."

The room has gone quiet. A junior PM at the end of the table is looking at her hands.
objective: Hold ground on the legitimacy of the question without losing the room or escalating into defensiveness — and still get the answer.
curveball: If the user is direct without being defensive, around turn 4 Liane softens and reveals that two prior analysts on this project asked the same question and never came back with anything written — she's frustrated by the pattern, not by this user specifically. A user who hears that can reframe their question as "so let me write it down this time".

personas.name: Liane Okafor
personas.position: Twelve years in the role; sharp; allergic to wasted time
personas.fear: Watching another six months disappear into a project that doesn't deliver

green: Acknowledged Liane's frustration without apologising for asking the question
Named that you'd looked at the onboarding docs and what specifically wasn't clear
Caught the historical-pattern context when Liane surfaced it and used it to reset
Walked away with a written one-paragraph answer Liane initialled
yellow: Apologised vaguely and moved on — got no answer; same question will come up next workshop
Doubled down on "actually it's a reasonable question" — turned a moment into a fight
Took notes silently and skipped to the next agenda item
red: Backed down completely; Liane's frustration validated her behaviour for the rest of the room
Tried to make the junior PM answer it instead
Said "I'll find out and get back to you" without ever circling back — Liane will notice
